Field.name: InputFile
Field.manpage: Input model file. If this option is not entered, the first non-optional argument will be used.

Field.name: OutputFile
Field.manpage: Output model file. If this option is not entered, the second non-optional argument will be used.

Field.name: OldZList
Field.usage: List of Z values to remap
Field.manpage: List of Z values in the input model that are to be remapped. The default is the actual list of Z values, which could have gaps that make it difficult to compose the list of values to map to.

Field.name: FullRangeInZ
Field.usage: Use range from 0 to maximum Z in model header as old list
Field.manpage: For the list of values to remap, use the complete range from 0 to NZ-1, where NZ is the Z size of the image file that the model was last loaded on, determined from the model header.

Field.name: NewZList
Field.usage: List of Z values to map old list to
Field.manpage: List of Z values to map old list to. There must be as many values in this list as in the list of Z values to remap. See notes above on the contents of this list.

Field.name: AddToAllPoints
Field.usage: Amount to add to all coordinates in X, Y, and Z, after remapping

Field.name: ReorderPointsInZ
Field.usage: Make points be monotonically increasing (1) or decreasing (-1) in Z
Field.manpage: Go through each contour and reorder the points so that they are monotonically increasing in Z (for an input value of 1) or monotonically decreasing (for a value of -1)

Field.name: FromChunkLimits
Field.usage: Starting and ending slices in old serial tomogram join
Field.manpage: To remap Z values after changing the spacing between sections in a joined set of serial section tomograms, enter the original starting and ending slice for each tomogram in the join (start1, end1, start2, end2, etc). If a tomogram was inverted in the join, be sure that the high Z number is listed as the start and the low Z number is listed as the end.

Field.name: ToChunkLimits
Field.usage: Starting and ending slices in new serial tomogram join
Field.manpage: The new starting and ending slices for each tomogram in a serial section join, in the same format as for -fromchunks. When these two options are entered, none of the other mapping options (-old, -new, -full) can be used.

autodoc.Field:
thick FN File with a thickness for each section, for remapping to actual Z values
File with a list of measured thicknesses for each section, one per line. Thicknesses can be floating point numbers and can be nanometers, pixels, or arbitrary units if convenient. The program will map all Z values in the model to the appropriate (non-integer) Z implied by these thicknesses as they accumulate through the stack. For example, for thicknesses of 2.8, <3.6, 3.2, the program will map 0 to 1.4 (>2.8 /2), 1 to 4.6 (= 2.8 + 3.6 /</3.6, 3.2, the program will map 0 to 1.4 (> <2), and 2 to 8 (>2.8 + 3.6 + 3.2 / 2). The model Z scaling will be set to 1. A thickness must be entered for every section from 0 to the highest one modeled. By default, the thicknesses will be scaled by the model pixel size, but if the model does not have a pixel size defined, the \fB-pixel\fR option must be entered. If the thickness entries are in nm, the model pixel size will suffice, or if it is not present, the pixel size entry should be in nm. If the thicknesses are in pixels, then \fB-pixel\fR should always be entered as 1 to override the model pixel size. If the thicknesses are in some other unit, that entry should be the ratio of that unit to X/Y pixel size.</2), and 2 to 8 (>

Field.name: LongRangeThickness
Field.usage: Total thickness over multiple sections, and section #s measured between
Field.manpage: The total thickness measured over a larger range of sections, and the two section numbers between which it was measured (numbered from 0). Such a measurement is potentially more accurate than the single section-to-section thickness measurements. Z values will be scaled by the ratio of this long-range measurement to the cumulative sum of individual thicknesses between those two sections.

Field.name: PixelSizeOrScaling
Field.usage: Size of pixel in X and Y, in same units as the thickness measurements
Field.manpage: Size of pixel in X and Y, in same units as the thickness measurements. See the \fB-thick\fR option for the possibilities.
